source_snapshot: Baseline core library plus the exact downloader and mirror files fingerprinted below; isolated dependencies use the baseline pubspec constraints.

conditions.cache: Warm page cache from separate fixture preparation and verification; caches were not dropped.
conditions.host: Shared managed host; other tasks may run concurrently.
conditions.fixture_format: Synthetic opaque archive bytes; no decompression is invoked.
conditions.network: Mock HTTP client counts and rejects every request; all runs recorded zero requests.

metrics.peak_rss_bytes: ProcessInfo.maxRss process high-watermark, sampled when the operation future completes, before external hash validation. Includes runtime and all worker isolates.
metrics.operation_us: Stopwatch duration for downloadSplitToFile, including cached-part verification where needed.
metrics.cancel_latency_us: From setting cancellation at the first positive assembly report (4 MiB) until the operation future completes with cleanup.
metrics.cancellation_peak_scope: Cancellation processes start with identity sidecars but no verified marker, so peak includes fresh hashes of every cached part before assembly.
metrics.retry_peak_scope: Fresh retry process reuses retained verified parts, joins the entire archive, publishes, and cleans parts.
metrics.callbacks_after_completion: Checked after allowing the event loop another 20 ms.
metrics.thresholds: No RSS or timing pass/fail threshold; correctness assertions determine passed.

verification: Every cancellation reports PatchDownloadCancelled, preserves all three parts and identity sidecars, and leaves neither the destination nor .joining.
A separate Python process streams SHA-256 over every retained part before retry.
Retry runs in a new AOT process, makes zero HTTP requests, publishes the expected size/hash, and removes part payloads and resume sidecars.
A separate Python process verifies the final archive SHA-256 and joined identity.
Every run records zero progress callbacks or cancellation checks after publication, and zero progress callbacks after future completion.

reproduce.repeat: Use a fresh fixture directory for each repetition and replace 64 with 256 for the larger case. Run cancel and retry as separate AOT processes. Remove only owned fixtures after validation.
reproduce.source_fingerprint: The fixture generator records the downloader source SHA-256. Build and prepare from the same unchanged source snapshot.
reproduce.windows_note: The generated executable uses the .exe suffix on Windows; these recorded results are Linux only.
reproduce.space: Allow at least twice the fixture size plus headroom, because retained parts and staging coexist.

limitations: Two repetitions per case are diagnostics, not statistical tail-latency guarantees.
tmpfs and warm cache do not represent slow storage, removable media, antivirus, or Windows behavior.
Peak RSS is a platform-dependent process metric and is not Dart heap size.
The probe covers cached-part assembly/cancellation/resume, not network transfer or ZSTD extraction.
Native SHA implementations on Windows/macOS were not exercised.
